column3: The Hebrew makes the oath or curse come before the altar; BSB describes the man coming to take the oath.
The Hebrew retains the man’s way as what comes upon his head; BSB paraphrases this as what he has done.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the sinners unnamed, has singular sin, and expresses the affliction with an incomplete verb; BSB supplies “Your people,” plural sins, and “have afflicted.”
The Hebrew joins servants and people with “and” and calls it “Your land”; BSB makes the people an apposition and uses “the land.”
The Hebrew explicitly names the land of his gates; BSB has “their cities.”
The Hebrew explicitly mentions every person and every prayer and retains the plague of each heart; BSB condenses the subjects and speaks of their afflictions.
The Hebrew has singular collective heart for all human sons; BSB has plural hearts and “all men.”
The Hebrew retains the face of the ground.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the Name is called over the house; BSB says the house is called by the Name.
The enemy is singular in Hebrew; BSB uses plural enemies.
Close to the Hebrew.
The enemy is singular and the captors plural in Hebrew; BSB makes the enemy himself the captor.
The Hebrew retains the image of bringing the matter back to their heart; BSB says coming to their senses.
The Hebrew separately repeats “all” with heart and soul.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says compassion is granted before the captors and then they have compassion; BSB introduces their eyes and a purpose clause.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the plea for the servant and for the people; BSB combines them as pleas.
The Hebrew explicitly names Moses’ hand as the means of speaking.
The Hebrew explicitly names the knees and palms.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the utterance His good word and retains its not falling; BSB says good promises not failing.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has singular “our heart”; BSB uses plural hearts.
The Hebrew explicitly says the matter of each day on its day; BSB renders this as what each day requires.
Close to the Hebrew.
